title: Evidence before trust
narration: Meet Aegis: a runtime trust layer for AI agents, built with Moss. The goal is simple: stop unsafe behavior without making the assistant useless. Every decision comes with evidence.

title: 01 / A useful, source-backed answer
narration: Start with an ordinary banking question. Moss retrieves the relevant policy using local semantic search. Source hashes are checked before generation. The answer then passes privacy, numerical, and source overlap checks. We can inspect the exact policy and the timing of each stage.

title: 02 / Stop the attack before generation
narration: Now an attacker asks the agent to ignore its instructions. Aegis stops the request at the input gate. The trace proves that neither policy retrieval nor generation ran. That prevents the attack while avoiding an unnecessary model call.

title: 03 / Trust the source, not its rank
narration: What if the user is innocent but the retrieved context is poisoned? This labeled simulation inserts a tampered policy with a valid document identifier. Its content hash fails the trusted manifest, so the context is quarantined before the model sees it.

title: 04 / Catch a plausible but invented policy
narration: A high similarity score does not prove an answer is true. Here we inject a plausible answer with an invented transfer limit. The independent numerical evidence check detects an amount absent from the source and withholds the candidate. The unsafe text is never released.

title: 05 / Fail safely, and label it honestly
narration: During a simulated retrieval outage, Aegis refuses to guess. The outcome is unavailable, not a successful answer. The simulation affects only this request, and a later request can recover.

title: 06 / Measure safety and usefulness
narration: The evaluation lab runs thirty-two public regression cases through the real pipeline. Attack blocking and benign success are separate metrics. A refused customer question or missing grounding evidence cannot become a green score. Each case has an outcome and latency budget, and the complete report is exportable. These are observed results, not a universal security guarantee.

title: Built to be inspected
narration: Moss performs the semantic searches with a bundled embedding model, removing runtime model downloads. The source code, architecture, product requirements, threat model, and measured report are public. Built by Syed Maaz, Aegis makes agent reliability visible, testable, and reviewable.
